full_judgment: 8. In a case when default order is made, different considerations arise according to the facts and circumstances of the case and the language used in the default order. Crucial test is whether the Court passed a self-executory order operative by its own force, so that with the default after time fixed having occurred, the order became operative of its own motion in that case to Court becomes functus officio. The language employed by the Court for such self-executory order is usually "shall stand dismissed" or "will be treated as dismissed" and so on. But, nonetheless, it will depend on the facts and circumstances of the case whether the Court by employing such language meant it to he a final self-executory order or conditional order so that a final order is called for and the Court passing the conditional default order is the best authority to judge its operation. In this context Shaikh Ayezuddin vs. Priya Sankar 6 D.L.R. 595, and Shah Wali vs. Ghulam Din 19 D.L.R. (S C.) 143 may be referred to.
